5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 5

Adverbs of frequency

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Say how often we do things (con qué frecuencia)
  • Learn always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely and never
  • Put the adverb in the right place in the sentence
  • Ask and answer How often…? with once, twice and every
  • Ask Do you ever…? and answer with short answers
  • Review the present simple with he, she and it
  • Describe a daily routine and report the results of a survey

Para pensar

¿Te lavas los dientes todos los días? ¿Comes brócoli de vez en cuando? ¿Has subido a un camello alguna vez? ¿Cómo dirías en inglés con qué frecuencia haces algo?

Explicación

1. How often?

Adverbs of frequency tell us how often something happens. We use them with the present simple to talk about routines and habits: «I always have breakfast at eight.» «My cat never drinks milk.» «We sometimes go to the cinema.»

Imagine a scale from 100% to 0%. At the top is always, the thing you do every single time. At the bottom is never, the thing you don't do at all. In the middle there are other words. En castellano: son palabras como «siempre», «a menudo» o «nunca».

2. Six adverbs

Let's learn them with examples. always (siempre, 100%): «I always wear a seatbelt in the car.» usually (normalmente, 80%): «I usually walk to school.» often (a menudo, 60%): «We often play basketball at break.»

sometimes (a veces, 40%): «My dad sometimes cooks pizza.» rarely or hardly ever (casi nunca, 10%): «I rarely watch the news.» never (nunca, 0%): «Penguins never fly.» Pronunciación: often se dice «ófen» (la t casi no suena) y usually, «iúshuali».

3. Hardly ever and other adverbs

Besides the six main adverbs, there are a few more that are very common:

  • hardly ever (casi nunca, about 5%): «I hardly ever watch horror films.» It means the same as rarely, but it is more common in conversation.
  • normally (normalmente): similar to usually. «I normally have lunch at school.»
  • frequently (frecuentemente): similar to often, but more formal.
  • occasionally (de vez en cuando): similar to sometimes. «We occasionally eat out.»
  • seldom (rara vez): it means the same as rarely, but it is old-fashioned and very formal.

Here is the complete scale, from 100% to 0%:

always → usually / normally → often → sometimes → occasionally → rarely / hardly ever → never

Careful with hardly ever: it has a negative meaning, so we don't use don't with it. «I hardly ever eat sweets», not «I don't hardly ever eat sweets».

The position rules are the same for all these adverbs: before the main verb («I hardly ever cry»), but after the verb to be («She is normally happy»). Occasionally, like sometimes, can also go at the beginning of the sentence: «Occasionally, we eat out.» A good idea is to draw the scale in your notebook with a colour for each adverb, from green (always) to red (never).

4. Where does the adverb go?

The position is important. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: «I always get up at seven.» «She often reads comics.» «They never eat meat.»

But with the verb to be, they go after it: «I am always hungry after PE.» «My brother is never late.» «We are usually tired on Fridays.» Truco: «antes del verbo de acción, después de be». En castellano tenemos más libertad, por eso es un error típico.

5. Sometimes and negatives

Sometimes is special: it can also go at the beginning or the end of the sentence. «Sometimes I go by bike.» «I go by bike sometimes.»

Never is already negative, so we don't use don't with it. ✔ «I never eat sweets at night.» ✘ «I don't never eat…». In negative sentences we can use don't usually or don't often: «I don't usually drink coffee» (normalmente no tomo café). En castellano: decimos «no como nunca», pero en inglés solo hay una negación.

6. Questions: How often…?

To ask about frequency we say How often…? + do/does: «How often do you go swimming?» «How often does your sister play the violin?»

We can answer with an adverb: «I sometimes go swimming.» Or with an expression of frequency: «Once a week» (una vez a la semana). «Twice a month» (dos veces al mes). «Three times a year» (tres veces al año). «Every day» (todos los días). «Every Saturday».

7. Do you ever…?

Another way to ask about habits is with ever (alguna vez): Do / Does + subject + ever + verb?

  • «Do you ever eat sushi?»
  • «Does your dad ever cook?»
  • «Are you ever late for school?» (with be, the question starts with Are / Is).

We can answer with a short answer and an adverb. Look at the position of the adverb: it goes before do, does, am, is or are in short answers:

  • «Yes, I sometimes do.» / «Yes, I often do.»
  • «Yes, he always does. He's a great cook!»
  • «No, I never do.» (Notice: with never, we don't say «don't».)
  • «No, I'm never late!»

We use ever in questions, but not in affirmative sentences: say «I sometimes eat sushi», not «I ever eat sushi».

To continue the conversation, ask a second question: «Do you ever go to the cinema?» – «Yes, I often do.» – «What kind of films do you like?» Good conversations are like a ball game: you answer, then you ask.

8. Once, twice, every…

Expressions of frequency are more exact than adverbs. once = one time; twice = two times; then three times, four times… + a day / a week / a month / a year.

We can also use every: every day, every morning, every weekend, every summer. These expressions usually go at the end of the sentence: «I have English three times a week.» «We visit my aunt every Christmas.» «I go to the dentist twice a year.»

9. Healthy routines

Adverbs of frequency are perfect to talk about habits. Are your habits healthy? «I always wash my hands before lunch.» «I usually sleep nine or ten hours.» «I often eat fruit.» «I sometimes eat chips.» «I rarely drink fizzy drinks.» «I never go to bed after eleven.»

Look at your week. Is there something you want to do more often? Something you want to do less often? Writing your routine in English helps you practise and think about your health at the same time.

10. Present simple review: he, she, it

Adverbs of frequency go with the present simple. Remember that with he, she and it we add -s to the verb: «She always plays the piano.» The adverb doesn't change anything.

Spelling rules for the third person:

  • Most verbs: add -s: play → plays, read → reads, eat → eats.
  • Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: add -es: watch → watches, wash → washes, go → goes, do → does.
  • Consonant + y: change to -ies: study → studies, fly → flies. But vowel + y: play → plays.
  • Irregular: have → has.

In negatives and questions, we use doesn't and does, and the verb loses the -s:

  • «He doesn't usually walk to school.» (not «doesn't walks»)
  • «Does she often go swimming?» (not «does she goes»)

Notice where the adverb goes in negatives: after doesn't / don't and before the verb: «I don't usually eat meat.»

11. Reading: a busy family

Read Joel's text: «My family is very busy. My mum is a nurse, so she often works at night. My dad always makes breakfast and takes us to school. My sister Clara plays the trumpet. She practises every day, and our neighbours are sometimes angry! I play football twice a week. On Sundays we usually visit my grandparents. We never watch TV at lunch because we talk. We rarely eat out, but once a month we have a pizza night.»

How often does Joel play football? Who always makes breakfast? What do they never do?

12. Let's practise: class survey

Make a class survey. Prepare five questions with How often…?: «How often do you read a book?», «How often do you eat vegetables?», «How often do you play video games?» Ask five classmates and write their answers in a table.

Then report the results: «Three people always eat vegetables. Two people rarely read books. Everybody plays video games sometimes!» Repaso: el adverbio va antes del verbo y después de be; never no lleva don't; las expresiones como twice a week van al final.

13. My daily routine

A routine is what we do every day, usually in the same order. These verbs and expressions are very useful to describe it:

  • Morning: wake up, get up, have a shower, get dressed, brush my teeth, have breakfast, go to school.
  • Afternoon: have lunch, do my homework, go to football / music / swimming, play with friends.
  • Evening: have dinner, watch TV, read a book, go to bed.

To tell the time, use at: «I usually get up at half past seven.» «I always have dinner at nine.»

To order your routine, use sequencing words: first, then, after that, finally. And remember: on weekdays and at the weekend your routine is probably different! «On weekdays I get up at 7:30, but at the weekend I usually get up at ten.»

Example: «I always wake up at seven. First, I have a shower and get dressed. Then I have breakfast: I usually have milk and toast. After that, I walk to school. In the afternoon, I often play basketball. Finally, I go to bed at half past nine. I never go to bed late on weekdays!»

14. Reporting a survey

After a class survey, it's time to report the results. To say how many people do something, use these expressions:

  • All of us / Everybody: 100%. «Everybody brushes their teeth every day.» (Notice: everybody + verb with -s.)
  • Most of us: more than half. «Most of us play video games at the weekend.»
  • Half of the class: 50%. «Half of the class walks to school.»
  • Some of us / A few of us: a small number. «A few of us play an instrument.»
  • Nobody: 0%. «Nobody goes to bed after eleven.» (nobody + verb with -s, and no «don't»).

You can also use numbers: «Twelve students often eat vegetables. Three students never read comics.»

Present your results with a bar chart: write the activities on one side and the number of students on the other. Then write a short conclusion: «Our class is quite healthy. Most of us eat fruit every day, but we sometimes go to bed late.»

Adverbs of frequency

Ejercicios

  1. Order from 100% to 0%: sometimes, never, always, often, usually, rarely.

  2. Put the adverb in place: «We go to the park.» (often)

  3. Put the adverb in place: «They are noisy.» (sometimes)

  4. Correct: «He watches never TV.»

  5. Translate: «Normalmente desayuno cereales.»

  6. Write in English: «una vez al mes».

  7. Make the question: «___ ___ do you play tennis?» — «Once a week.»

  8. Correct: «I don't never eat fish.»

  9. Write a sentence with «every Sunday».

  10. Write four sentences about your routine with four different adverbs.

  11. Order from 100% to 0%: never, usually, always, hardly ever, sometimes.

  12. Write the he/she form: watch, study, have, go, play.

  13. Short answer: «Do you ever eat fish?» (often)

  14. Write three things you do in the morning.

  15. Complete: «___ of the class walks to school.» (50%)

  16. Correct: «She doesn't usually goes to the park.»

  17. Write a question with ever about your teacher.

  18. Translate: «Casi nunca como dulces.»

  19. Write two sentences: one about weekdays and one about the weekend.

  20. How many sunrises can astronauts see every day?

  21. Write your daily routine in eight sentences with times, sequencing words and adverbs.

  22. Interview a family member and write their routine in the third person.

  23. Do a survey of ten classmates and report the results with most of us, half, a few and nobody.

  24. Write five sentences comparing your routine with an astronaut's routine.

Practica

  1. «Always» means…

    1. A) nunca
    2. B) a veces
    3. C) siempre

  2. «Never» means…

    1. A) nunca
    2. B) a menudo
    3. C) casi siempre

  3. Which adverb is about 40%?

    1. A) usually
    2. B) sometimes
    3. C) always

  4. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) I walk usually to school.
    2. B) I usually walk to school.
    3. C) Usually I walk usually.

  5. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) She often is tired.
    2. B) Often she tired.
    3. C) She is often tired.

  6. «___ do you go swimming?» — «Twice a week.»

    1. A) How often
    2. B) How many
    3. C) When often

  7. «Twice» means…

    1. A) one time
    2. B) every time
    3. C) two times

  8. «I ___ eat meat.» (vegetarian)

    1. A) don't never
    2. B) never
    3. C) always

  9. «Rarely» is similar to…

    1. A) hardly ever
    2. B) usually
    3. C) often

  10. «He ___ plays chess.»

    1. A) sometimes
    2. B) sometime
    3. C) some times

  11. «Hardly ever» means…

    1. A) casi siempre
    2. B) casi nunca
    3. C) a menudo

  12. «Do you ever play tennis?» «Yes, I ___.»

    1. A) do sometimes play
    2. B) ever do
    3. C) sometimes do

  13. He ___ his teeth every day.

    1. A) brushs
    2. B) brushes
    3. C) brush

  14. «Nobody ___ to bed after eleven.»

    1. A) goes
    2. B) go
    3. C) doesn't go

  15. Astronauts sleep…

    1. A) in normal beds
    2. B) on the floor
    3. C) in sleeping bags on the wall

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué son los adverbios de frecuencia y su escala; Dónde se colocan en la frase con un verbo de acción y con to be; Por qué never no lleva don't; Cómo se pregunta y se responde con How often.

Soluciones

  1. C) 100 %.
  2. A) 0 %.
  3. B) A veces.
  4. B) Antes del verbo.
  5. C) Con be, después.
  6. A) Pregunta de frecuencia.
  7. C) Dos veces.
  8. B) Never sin don't.
  9. A) Casi nunca.
  10. A) Sometimes, junto.
  11. B) About 5%.
  12. C) Adverb + do.
  13. B) -sh + es.
  14. A) Nobody + -s.
  15. C) No gravity.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never.
  2. We often go to the park.
  3. They are sometimes noisy. (También: Sometimes they are noisy.)
  4. He never watches TV.
  5. I usually have cereal for breakfast.
  6. once a month.
  7. How often.
  8. I never eat fish.
  9. Model answer: We visit my grandma every Sunday.
  10. Model answer: I always brush my teeth. I usually walk to school. I sometimes read comics. I never eat chips for breakfast.
  11. always, usually, sometimes, hardly ever, never.
  12. watches, studies, has, goes, plays.
  13. Yes, I often do.
  14. Example: I get up, I have a shower, I have breakfast.
  15. Half.
  16. She doesn't usually go to the park.
  17. Example: Does our teacher ever sing in class?
  18. I hardly ever eat sweets.
  19. Example: On weekdays I get up at 7:30, but at the weekend I usually get up at ten.
  20. About sixteen.
  21. Open answer.
  22. Open answer with -s endings.
